title: HDR monotherapy for locally confined prostate cancer.
summary:
In patients with locally advanced prostate cancer, the aim is to demonstrate the tolerability and effectiveness of HDR monotherapy.
Brachytherapy has been an established treatment for patients with locally advanced prostate cancer for many years. Under ultrasound guidance, 
implantation needles are positioned within the prostate. Following evaluation of the treatment plan, the afterloading device is connected to the implantation needles and the irradiation is initiated. The irradiation procedure takes approximately 10 minutes. The needles are then removed from the patient.
In this procedure, the two treatments are administered one week apart.
The study aims to investigate the tolerability and efficacy of HDR monotherapy.

interventions.name: HDR brachytherapy, 2 fractions at 1 week intervals, each with a prescribed dose of 13.5 Gy

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with locally confined prostate cancer (cT1-2)
•    Gleason score 6-7a and ≤50% positive punch biopsy and PSA ≤20 ng/ml or
Gleason score 7b and ≤50% positive punch cylinder in biopsy and PSA <10 ng/ml  
•    Suitability for afterloading therapy (according to the clinic's own SOP)
•    No relevant obstruction symptoms (IPSS <18)
•    Age ≥18 years
•    Life expectancy > 10 years
•    Consent to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
• Local pre-treatment of prostate cancer (e.g. HiFU)
• TURP within the last 6 months
• Lithotomy position/anaesthesia not possible
• Implantation impaired by the pubic arch
• Legal incapacity or lack of consent
